title: One Test. Six ODIs. Seven T20Is. Two Tours. India's Next Sixty Days Are the Most Crowded in Cricket History.
excerpt: From Mullanpur to Chennai to Belfast to Lord's, India's post-IPL schedule is a marathon. Here is what every NRI cricket fan needs to know.
body:
The IPL is over. Royal Challengers Bengaluru have the trophy. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has the awards. And Indian cricket is already pivoting to the real work of 2026 — a relentless, continent-spanning schedule that will test squad depth, fitness, and scheduling like never before.

Between June 6 and July 19, India will play one Test, six ODIs, and seven T20Is across three countries, under two different captains, with two separate squads. It is, without exaggeration, the most compressed period of international cricket any team has attempted in the modern era.

Phase 1: Afghanistan at Home (June 6–20)

It begins in Mullanpur, a venue hosting its first-ever Test match. Shubman Gill captains a squad shorn of Jadeja, Axar Patel, and Jasprit Bumrah. KL Rahul is the vice-captain. Rishabh Pant keeps wicket.

The one-off Test (June 6–10) is not part of the World Test Championship cycle, but it matters. It is the only Test India will play for the remainder of 2026 before the Sri Lanka away series in August. For players like Gurnoor Brar and Harsh Dubey — both uncapped debutants in the Test squad — this is a once-in-a-generation opportunity.

The three ODIs follow immediately:

  • June 14: 1st ODI at HPCA Stadium, Dharamsala
  • June 17: 2nd ODI at Ekana Stadium, Lucknow
  • June 20: 3rd ODI at MA Chidambaram Stadium, Chennai

For the ODIs, the squad transforms. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli return. Shreyas Iyer takes the vice-captaincy. Hardik Pandya is back. It is an entirely different team in all but name — and the preparation for the 2027 World Cup begins in earnest.

Phase 2: Ireland Away (June 26–28)

The squad barely has time to unpack before flying to Belfast for two T20Is against Ireland at the Civil Service Cricket Club. These matches will likely feature India's younger T20I specialists — the format where Gill has struggled to cement his place and where new faces will audition for the England tour.

The Belfast games are day-night fixtures, starting at 4:30 PM local time (11:00 AM Eastern), making them among the most accessible for NRI viewers in North America.

Phase 3: England Away (July 1–19)

This is the centrepiece. Five T20Is and three ODIs across some of England's most storied grounds:

  • July 1: 1st T20I, Riverside Ground, Chester-le-Street
  • July 4: 2nd T20I, Old Trafford, Manchester
  • July 7: 3rd T20I, Trent Bridge, Nottingham
  • July 9: 4th T20I, County Ground, Bristol
  • July 11: 5th T20I, Rose Bowl, Southampton
  • July 14: 1st ODI, Edgbaston, Birmingham
  • July 16: 2nd ODI, Sophia Gardens, Cardiff
  • July 19: 3rd ODI, Lord's, London

The England tour is the proving ground for India's 2027 World Cup squad. Gill's form in English conditions — where he struggled during the Test series earlier this year — will be under intense scrutiny. For Kohli and Rohit, these ODIs may be among the last auditions before the World Cup squad is finalised.

The NRI Viewing Guide

For fans in North America, the timing works well for most matches. India's home ODIs start at 1:30 PM IST (4:00 AM Eastern, 1:00 AM Pacific) — early but manageable for the dedicated. The England fixtures are afternoon starts in BST, translating to morning or late-morning viewing in the US.

JioStar holds the broadcast rights for India's international cricket. In the US, matches are typically available on Willow TV and the JioCinema app. In the UK, Sky Sports carries the home England matches.

What to Watch For

The Gill-Gambhir dynamic: Head coach Gautam Gambhir and captain Gill have had a public-facing harmony, but the dropped players — Jadeja, Axar — suggest tough conversations are happening behind the scenes. How the pair manage a young, inexperienced squad under pressure will define India's next two years.

The World Cup auditions: With the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa and Zimbabwe, every ODI from here is a selection trial. Players like Ishan Kishan, Prince Yadav, and Gurnoor Brar are competing for spots that could define their careers.

Format transition fitness: The real question is not talent — India have plenty. It is whether the human body can sustain T20 intensity in the IPL, switch to Test cricket in four days, then fly to Europe for white-ball cricket, all within sixty days. England and Australia have lost players to burnout trying far less.

India's approach — send everyone, manage nothing, hope for the best — will either work spectacularly or produce the kind of injury and fatigue crisis that forces a rethink. Either way, NRI cricket fans are in for the most compelling two months of Indian cricket since the 2023 World Cup.
author: Diaspora Desk
